To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a Personal Health Recommenders System (PHRS).

the PHRS is a patient-centered, patient-centric system that combines personal health data, crowdsourced information, and domain ontologies, in a modular fashion that allows for easy integration of new ontologies and new sources of data, and that can evolve as the patient's medical condition changes over time.
the PHRS architecture is based on a patient's personal electronic health records, augmented by crowdsourced data and curated ontologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a PHRS that can be used to assist patients and healthcare providers with treatment decisions.
the design of a PHRS that is based on an integrated architecture of a PEHR, crowdsourced data and ontologies, and that is augmented with Semantic Web services.
the design, implementation and testing of a PHRS that incorporates the patient's PEHR, crowdsourced data, and Semantic Web services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PHRS is a novel architecture that combines a PEHR and a modular, patient-specific ontology, with crowdsourced data and authoritative resources.
the PEHR, augmented with crowdsourced data and authoritative ontologies, is an effective means to provide a patient with the best course of care.
the PHRS will be an effective and valuable tool for patients and healthcare professionals alike.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a PHRS is a patient-centered approach to managing personal health data that is based on an individual patient's PEHR, augmented by data crowdsourced from other patients, and classified according to authoritative domain ontologies.
the PHRS architecture combines a PEHR, crowdsourced data, and ontological reasoning, in order to provide the best possible recommendations to patients and healthcare providers.
we are proposing a novel PHRS architecture that is patient-centric, and which combines personal health records, crowdsourced data, and curated domain ontological data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a patient's personal health record can become the focal point of an intelligent system that can be used to recommend the best treatments for a patient's illness, based on the patient's symptoms, diagnoses, and treatment history, and the treatment histories and best practices of others who have had the same or similar illnesses.
a PHRS may be constructed from a patient's personal health records, and augmented with authoritative ontologies and crowdsourced data.
a PHRS can be constructed by integrating the PEHR, authoritative sources and ontologies, and crowdsourced data, all of which can be accessed via Semantic Web Services.
